steps.content: [Inside the Lighthouse]
A loud thud echoes as you land hard on the floor, hands and feet tightly bound.
This place appears to be a space beneath the lighthouse. The air is thick and humid, heavy with the cloying stench of decay and salt.

Your captor stands guard at the room's only exit, a grim silhouette holding back the nightmare outside. The Tide Crawlers, driven inland by the storm, slam against the doors and windows. Their frenzied scrabbling and hungry, vicious laughter are a grotesque chorus beneath the roar of thunder and crashing waves.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Answer me. Who are you?

Her voice is a blade. You can't see her face in the gloom, but her malice is a physical force. The back of your hand, where her boot pressed you into the shore, throbs in time with your heartbeat, the pain sharpened by the rough rope chafing against the wound.
Given the current diplomatic climate, revealing yourself as <color=#fb9259>the MBCC Chief</color> might not be the best card to play.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Speak!
I can tell by your accent you're from DisCity. So am I. I was with a WhiteSands merchant caravan. Our group got caught in a sandstorm. I woke up in the sea outside.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: A caravan?
She takes a threatening step closer, clearly not convinced by your answer.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Prove it.
[Lightning and thunder]
The thunderstorm rages on, lightning briefly illuminating the room's interior.
I can. But you've got my hands tied. I can't reach it.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: I'll get it. Where?
In the left pocket of my coat.
She crouches before you and begins to search your pocket. You force your breathing to stay even, a fragile mask for the frantic drumming of your heart.
It doesn't take long. Her hand withdraws clutching a clump of letter paper, swollen and pulpy from its soak in the Black Tide.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: What is it?
A letter. From a friend. She went exploring in WhiteSands; I joined the caravan to look for her. If you look at the smudged part, she always drew a little mouse there—ugh!
Before you can finish your sentence, a heavy blow slams into your ribs. The air explodes from your lungs, and you curl involuntarily into a ball on the floor, gasping.
She stuffs the soggy wad of <color=#fb9259>evidence</color> down your collar, then mockingly pats your cheek.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: You think I want a story?
You're the one who asked...
You swallow back the acid rising in your throat, struggling to recover.
I have more evidence. Right pocket.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Last chance.
She moves over you, crouching close on your other side. As if on cue, a flash of lightning bleaches the sky, illuminating the room.
Using the thunder's roar as cover, you coil your legs and kick out violently, aiming for her abdomen.

She has neither noticed your movement nor expected you to have any fight left. As she jerks back to dodge, her balance fails. The back of her head cracks sickeningly against the table corner you'd spotted.

She lets out a pained grunt. Ignoring the burn of the ropes, you wrench your wrists apart, feeling the bindings give way. You lunge forward, palm thrust out. Dizziness washes over you, but you grit your teeth against it. This power is your only leverage.
The spikes of dark light surge for her throat. But a knife is already at your neck, its cold point pressed to your artery.
The room falls quiet as darkness reclaims your vision.

You heard no draw, saw no glint of steel. She was simply faster... but how? Before you can even process this, the blade has already broken your skin, filling the air with the metallic scent of your own blood.
My <color=#fb9259>caravan</color> is still searching for me. They can confirm my identity.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Still lying... You're out of chances...
Believe what you want. But if you kill me, my companions will hunt you down.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: You think that will scare me?

She shoves you back, pinning your shoulders against the wall. In the utter blackness, you feel her warm breath rapid against your ear. Under the pretense of holding the blade, she has pressed her body against yours, her arm a heavy weight across your chest.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Enough talk. I'm ending this now!
You don't sound well.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: SHUT UP!!!

A furious roar rips from her throat as she pins you in the corner, her full weight crushing you. She torques your arms into sickening, unnatural angles, and the pop of dislocating joints fills the air.

Yet, within the blinding pain, your thoughts become icily clear. You notice the violent tremor in her muscles, the scorching heat radiating from her body. This violent reaction is far beyond anything your limited strength could have provoked.
She's holding something back.
Then why save me? If you pulled me from the sea, why kill me now?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: I said... shut up...
You control the lighthouse, don't you? If it's safe inside, why were you out there? What were you doing?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: None of your ******* business!
You don't care if I live or die, do you? You only care about who I am... You're waiting for someone.

options: You were trying to see if I was them.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: NO!!! I'm not waiting for anyone! NOBODY IS COMING!

She stabs downward in fury, but the blade veers wildly into the wall beside you. She can no longer control her own body. Her gaze seems to fix on your neck, her breath scorching the air as the sweet, drawing ever closer.
The metallic scent of your blood fills the space between you.
I don't know who you're waiting for, but I know what you're afraid of.
It's the smell of blood, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: I'LL KILL YOU!
You can't. Not in this state. And I can't fight back. So tell me what you're waiting for. Maybe I can help.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: You're in no position to bargain!
Aren't I?

You tighten your grip on the knife, hot blood welling between your fingers, its metallic tang thick in the air. She tries to protest, but her strength is gone; she's drawn to your blood-soaked hand like an addict beyond resistance.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Let go... how... how dare you...
Let's try a different question. What's your name? Who are you?
With a final, desperate lurch, she wrenches the blade free and shoves you back into the corner. In the darkness, you hear only her ragged, greedy breaths, followed by the wet, swallowing sound.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: You think you've won? Heh... Fine. Wait for your <color=#fb9259>companions</color>... it's no different than waiting to die!

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: I smelled your other wounds from the start. I know what those sea beasts do. There's barely a piece of you left that's not mangled!

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: None of us will see the morning!
With a resounding crash of iron, she is gone, disappearing in the downpour outside.

Silence descends, broken only by the relentless rain and the frantic rhythm of your own heartbeat. You count silently in the dark—one, two, all the way to five hundred—and only when you are certain she won't return do you finally exhale.

The tension drains from you, and with it, all your strength. Your limbs become dead weights as a deep, penetrating cold seeps up from the floor beneath you. By the weak moonlight, you examine your hands: the fingers are stained dark, the joints already locking in the chill.
Too bad for her. Interrogation is where I excel.
You can hardly believe you had the strength left to face her down. Your mind winnows down to a primal checklist: warmth, water, treatment, food... survival.
Shivering violently, you fumble your way around the circular room. Everything is damp, rotten. But by some miracle, your fingers close around a small, dry box. Matches.
An antiquated design, even for Syndicate.

The match flares, casting a dancing light on the cloud of your breath and reveals a small, iron stove. The fire you coax to life is too meager to heat the room or truly warm you, but its glow is a sanctuary.
You huddle before it, tearing strips from the hem of your coat to fashion crude bandages. Without medicine, stemming the bleeding is the only battle you can win tonight.
I should really wash this coat. Hecate and Nightingale will freak out if they see all these bloodstains.

You wonder when you'll leave this place and when you'll see them again... You force yourself to focus on warm memories to keep your emotions in check, knowing that in your situation, a backlash from the Black Ring would only cause more trouble.
Above, rain drips steadily through the cracked dome; the wind moans around the lighthouse walls. The coppery smell of blood is slowly being lost to the damp, musty odor of decay.
The smell that drove her away.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: None of us will see the morning.
Her sentence hangs in the air, cold and incontestable. This lighthouse, this sea, this lonely island—you still have no explanation for any of it.
You tuck the crumpled ball of "evidence" safely into your pocket, wrap the tattered coat around yourself, and stare into the flames.
I have to survive. I wasn't lying... This is a letter from Hella. I have to find her. I can't... I can't fall here. Not until I know she's safe.
A fragile sense of warmth finally blossoms in your chest, and with it comes an irresistible tide of fatigue, your eyelids growing heavier by the second.
Your body betrays you, slumping against the cold wall as you sink into a deep and dreamless sleep.
[Screen fades to black] [Sound of crackling stove continues briefly]
[Coast]

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: ...Bastard! I'll kill him! I'll kill him!
steps.female_content: ...Bastard! I'll kill her! I'll kill her!

steps.content: She hurls herself into the horde of monsters crawling ashore. Fangs tear into her shoulder, ripping a chunk from her coat.
Rain and seawater stream down her arm, mingling with the blood on her hands—the blood from the person inside the house. It's still warm, carrying a sweetness that has no place here.
Her alien blade—like a grotesque fusion of bone and metal—hisses through the rain, tearing through the monster tide with eerie whispers. It cuts faster and faster, an unstoppable frenzy.

She and the Tide Crawlers savage one another, contamination fluid drenching her completely. She does not retreat, her humanity lost to a feral madness. In the darkness, she is a monster among monsters.
Her voice is a raw, inhuman shriek, as if the sound of the blade itself speaks through her.

steps.speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
steps.content: Damn it... I've had enough of this.
